findings: Requested prefix and short reads are handled by the original helper.
Early EOF returns short successful length; caller must validate promised length.
A zero buffer length on an empty thread-local buffer returns zero bytes despite nonempty input.
Largest per-thread buffer remains retained after smaller requests.
scope: Original scan and TLS block executed verbatim with primitive FileLen adapter; default FileHasher buffer is nonzero 65536. Zero-buffer control is helper contract boundary, not normal CLI failure. Early EOF is documented at-most stream behavior; no whole scanner mutation race or bad duplicate group claim.
